_comment: Claude Code registration of the shared, provider-neutral Python hooks (.claude/hooks/*.py speak every provider payload via _compat.py). The Codex counterpart (.codex/hooks.json + config.toml) is GENERATED from this file by team-kits/gen_provider_artifacts.py - never hand-maintained. Every interpreter runs with -B: .claude/hooks and .claude/kernel are the hashed enforcement bundle, and a hook that leaves a .pyc behind changes the bundle it was just trusted against - which is why bytecode used to be excluded from the hash instead (kernel/hashing.py BYTECODE_SUFFIXES). Measured cost of -B on a full kernel import: ~5 ms. The `model` key is the project's DEFAULT model, and it names the same tier the bound `agent` carries so the kit does not ship two answers to the question which model this session runs on. Measured 2026-08-21 (docs/reviews/2026-08-21-tsk0078-measurements.md): the bound agent's own `model:` frontmatter WINS over this key, and an explicit user model choice wins over both -- so this value governs only what names no model of its own. Every shipped role does (tools/validate.py refuses a specialist or a lead without `model:`), which leaves the Codex lead fallback in gen_provider_artifacts and any built-in agent.

PreToolUse._comment: A `timeout` ON A REGISTRATION IS A KILL WINDOW, and a killed gate is a silent allow -- so an entry may name one only where the hook refuses BEFORE it, and must name one where the hook cannot finish inside the default. Measured 2026-08-23 on claude.exe 2.1.239 (tools/provider_observations.json -> hook_deadlines): an entry with `timeout: 5` whose hook needed 20 s was KILLED and the refused command RAN, with nothing on the user's channel to say a gate had been killed; an entry naming NO timeout survived 310 s and 560 s and was killed at 900 s, so a default window exists too and sits near 600 s. Three entries here carried 60/120 on the assumption that a window HELPS a gate that has no bound of its own -- it does the opposite, and they lost it. `gate_pipeline` is the one that KEEPS a window: it bounds its own child at 1500 s and that is longer than the default kill, so without a larger registered window a long suite would be killed at ~600 s and the refused push would go through -- 1800 > 1500 is what makes its own refusal arrive first. `tools/test_hooks.py::test_a_registration_names_a_window_exactly_when_its_gate_can_outlive_the_default` measures the rule off the shipped file and off each gate's own code. What no window buys back is a hook that hangs inside its own process: nothing in `_compat` notices a deadline, so `_compat.HOOK_DEADLINE_SECONDS` is a budget the hooks give themselves and not one anything enforces.

ONE chained command, and gate_dispatch is LAST because it is the only one here that SPENDS something (the task's dispatch lease). Measured 2026-08-02: every PreToolUse hook of an event runs to completion even when a sibling exits 2, so registered separately this gate paid for spawns the gates beside it were refusing in the same 52 ms. _gate.py runs the chain in one process and stops at the first refusal. The timeout is the whole chain's, so it carries the largest the separate registrations carried.

SubagentStop._comment: ONE chained command, and gate_dispatch is LAST because the gate ahead of it can turn this stop into a CONTINUATION: gate_subagent_output exits 2 for a final message without its output contract, and the child then keeps working. gate_dispatch records the child's END here (BUG-0058), and a record written ahead of that refusal would report a specialist that is still running as idle at the lead's next turn-end. _gate.py runs the chain in one process and stops at the first refusal, which is exactly what makes the order carry the meaning.

Stop._comment: The way back for a dispatch lease that was spent on a spawn nobody ever started. `PermissionDenied` used to carry that job and was removed here: measured 2026-08-02, it fired in NONE of twelve real headless sessions, on either a hook refusal or a permission refusal, while PostToolUseFailure from this same file did fire. Stop fired in all twelve, including after four refused tool calls. gate_dispatch DOES exit 2 here, for one thing and no other: a dispatch whose own records say no child is on it, which the lead was about to leave unmentioned for another turn (BUG-0058). A Stop that exits 2 does not end the turn, which is the right answer to that and the wrong one to a rollback - so the reconciliation beside it stays silent. It refuses at most once per finding and never on a stop the provider marks as one a hook already blocked - see handle_stop and _name_the_dispatches_the_records_say_nobody_is_on.
